This isn't right - `completionCode` is not written between its initialisation and this test.

I think you rather want to test `event_receive_resp_data.completion_code`?
True.

The grammar here doesn't seem quite right, can you rework it?

Also, it's not a failure to decode if `rc` is 0 but `event_receiver_resp_data.completion_code` is not `PLDM_SUCCESS` - that's a failure on the part of the command semantics at the terminus.
I've reworded it to be a more general error that covers both.
can we use placement new operator here?
Done

Although this is not lg2 log, but we should not use `Anti-pattern`.
" error = {errorValue}".
`only, rc = " << rc` ==> `only, return code " << rc`

Thanks for the review @thu@os.amperecomputing.com I did not find this antipatern neither in the pldm docs repo or the phosphor-logging.
Can you point to a source that explains this antipatern, please?

I think it's all about writing logs that are human-readable. (https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/anti-patterns.md#ill-defined-data-structuring-in-lg2-message-strings). Even though the anti-pattern talks about lg2, its better to write logs which does not have acronyms.
Acknowledged
Don't use `Anti-pattern` when prints message.
Acknowledged
Change to use c++ type casting.
Acknowledged

return code = " -> return code "

"return code=" -> "return code "
",completion code=" -> " ,completion code "

I've updated the messages with the last feedback, however I have a concern that we are not defining a proper "standard" way of doing things in the tool.

Shall I push a separate commit that fixes all other existing occurrences of ill formed error messages ( the one's that use rc=X, cc=X), or are we going to maintain the inconsistency in the tool?

Same with the C++ casting style or the placement new vs struct casting.
sure, please feel free to do so.
